text:
Alexander: Heads up — ALB target group tg-edge-usw2 is flipping unhealthy -> healthy repeatedly, and targets are getting deregistered for short windows (few mins). Seeing a big spike starting ~10:15 UTC.

infra-bot: alert: ALB health check failures detected for tg-edge-usw2 (CloudWatch link: https://console.aws.amazon.com/cloudwatch/home) — 10m spike 504/timeout

Maria: Which node pool / subnet? edge or core? Any recent deploys?

Alexander: This is the edge pool in us-west-2 (edge-pool-a). No app deploys at that time. Health check path is /healthz (HTTP 200 normally). From the node I can curl the pod IP and get 200, but ALB still reports timeout/504.

Chris: Can you paste the target group config and recent target health output?

Alexander: Config: (aws cli output)
```
TargetGroupArn: arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-west-2:...:targetgroup/tg-edge-usw2
HealthCheckProtocol: HTTP
HealthCheckPath: /healthz
HealthCheckIntervalSeconds: 10
HealthCheckTimeoutSeconds: 5
HealthyThresholdCount: 3
UnhealthyThresholdCount: 2
```
and `aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn ...` showed many targets in "unhealthy (timeout)" during the spike.

Maria: Do the pods show Ready=false at that same time? kubelet events?

Alexander: Yes — kube-probe/readiness is flapping at the same timestamps. Kubelet logs show repeated connection failures and I found repeated conntrack warnings in dmesg: "nf_conntrack: table full".

Sung: That screams conntrack / SNAT exhaustion. When ALB health checks come from outside, connections get DNAT->pod via kube-proxy; ephemeral ports + conntrack entries can blow out. Check `conntrack -L | wc -l` and `sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max`. Also check ip_local_port_range and NAT Gateway/ENI capacity.

Alexander: Ran checks: `conntrack -L | wc -l` => 65536 (at limit). `sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max` => 65536. ip_local_port_range = 32768 61000. NAT GW metrics: no obvious drop but NAT gateway connection tracking at the subnet edge could be saturating. I temporarily bumped nf_conntrack_max to 200000 on one node and the flapping stopped for that node.

Chris: Where are health checks terminating — ALB -> node -> kube-proxy -> pod, or ALB -> pod IP directly (ip target)? If using instance targets with kube-proxy DNAT, connection churn is heavier. Consider switching TG to IP targets or use target-type=ip so ALB talks directly to pod IPs (if allowed).

Alexander: We're using instance targets for historical reasons (CNI didn't support target-type=ip for this cluster when it was created). Switching target type requires careful rollout. For short term, increasing conntrack & adjusting ip_local_port_range looks lower-risk. Also adding a dedicated lightweight /lb-health endpoint that bypasses sidecar could reduce probe overhead.

oncall-rotation: Recommendation: don't hotpatch all nodes manually. Plan: 1) create DaemonSet that sets sysctl at boot (or use privileged init to apply /etc/sysctl.d/99-conntrack.conf), 2) cordon & drain nodes in small batches in edge-pool-a, 3) apply conntrack_max increase + adjust ip_local_port_range + add alert if conntrack > 80%, 4) explore TG target-type=ip in staging and test. I'll open a runbook. :white_check_mark:

Alexander: Implementing step 1 on a test node now. Command I ran: `sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=200000` and `sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range=\"15000 65000\"`. After that node's health stabilized.

infra-bot: deploy: rolling sysctl daemonset rollout started for edge-pool-a at 1763509200

Chris: After the test node, ALB showed stable healthy states for that target. Good find. Let's add a CloudWatch metric alarm for TargetGroupUnhealthyHostCount and conntrack usage.

Sung: Also check conntrack timeout values, and consider moving ALB health checks to TCP or shorter path that doesn't involve auth/sidecar to minimize backend work.

Alexander: Opening infra ticket INFRA-2147 to track: daemonset sysctl, NAT gateway scaling investigation, target-type migration plan, and monitoring alerts. Rolling patch scheduled tomorrow at 03:00 UTC to avoid traffic.

Chris: Thanks — please add rollback steps (revert sysctl and drain rollback). After this we should also document why instance-targets -> DNAT increases conntrack pressure. :thumbsup:

oncall-rotation: Note: after change we'll also update oncall runbook with steps to check `conntrack -L | wc -l`, `ss -s`, and ALB target health.

Alexander: Confirmed: patch rolled on test node, ALB target healthy; will proceed with controlled rollout.

Chris: Great work everyone.
